227 GPS Permanent Station and Seismological Observatory to......
Twenty Fourth Indian Antarctic Expedition 2003-2005
Ministry of Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 22, pp 227-238
Contributions of GPS Permanent Station and
Seismological Observatory to Geophysical Studies
at Maitri, Antarctica During
XXIV-Indian Antarctic Expedition
A. Nageswara Rao, S.V .R. Ramachandra Rao, G.B. Navinchander,
A. Akilan, G.S. Srinivas, E.C. Malaimani and N. Ravikumar
National Geophysical Research Institute, Uppal Road, Hyderabad-500 007, India
ABSTRACT
On going research activities at Antarctica were successfully carried out during
XXIV IAE for the long-term scientific objectives of NGRI. The data from GPS
station continues to contribute to Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research
(SCAR) and International Earth Rotation Service (IERS). The seismological
observatory continues to contribute to NEIC (USGS), ISC, (UK) and plays a pivotal
role in the Global Seismographic Network in Antarctica. Global positioning system
(GPS) measurements at Maitri, Indian Antarctic station, have been carried out for
the period 1997 to date. The International GPS Service for Geodynamics (IGS)
stations, in different plates, such as Casey, Davis, Kerguelen, Seychelles, Coco,
Hartebeesthoek, Yaragadee, and Tidbinbilla were chosen for global network
solution. The GPS data from 1997 to 2005 of all these IGS stations in and around
Antarctica along with Maitri were used to estimate the time series, baseline lengths
and their changes and velocity vectors of individual sites. The results have enabled
to obtain a deeper insight into the driving mechanism and the causative factors for
Indian plate kinematics. During this expedition i.e., from January 2005 to February
2006, continuous seismic data were also acquired for processing and analysis. The
final analysis of this data has been completed using SEISAN software and reported
to ISC, United Kingdom as per their time schedule up to December 2005. The
number of earthquakes recorded as global events and near-events in and around
Antarctica during the period of expedition is discussed in this report.
INTRODUCTION
Focused study on the Indian Ocean and South Sandwich Islands
Region becomes very important in the present scenario of interplate and
intraplate earthquakes that do occur frequently in India and nearby regions,
228 A. Nageswara Rao et al.
forcing us to re-evaluate the rigidity of the Indian plate as well as Indian
Ocean Margin. GPS-Geodesy and Seismic Studies are extended to envelop
the large Indian Ocean lithosphere. In order to monitor the seismic activity
in and around Antarctica and Indian Ocean, a reconnaissance survey for
site selection and feasibility of operation of seismological observatory in
Antarctica was initiated during 16
th Indian Antarctic Expedition and a Digital
Short Period System was installed during 17th expedition. The station was
fully commissioned on 26 January 1998 with analog and short period digital
systems. This observatory was further upgraded with the installation of
Broadband seismic system during the 20
th IAE, comprising a Broadband
Sensor CMG-3ESP (GURALP make with 50 Hz to 100 sec flat response)
and Reftek Data Acquisition System.
The permanent seismic station at Maitri has gone global by figuring
in AnSWeR. (Antarctic Seismic Web Resource) as shown in Figure 4, with
the station code MAIT. After final analysis of seismic broad band digital
data, the complete phase data had been reported to ISC, to be included in
the global data center for global access by any other agency and can be
accessed at: 
http://www.isc.ac.uk
The Seismic sensors (S-13 for short period  & analog recorders and
Guralp CMG-3ESP for Broadband System) have been installed in the
underground vault behind Tirumala Hut. The Data Acquisition System
(DAS) – REFTEK High Resolution Digital Data Acquisition System RT
72A 121-03 from Refraction Technology Inc., USA interfaced with a P.C.,
Analog Recorder – vertical component analog RV-320B Portacorder and a
GPS receiver –was installed in the Tirumala hut. The Sensor pit and the lab
are being maintained at about 15 to 20 degrees temperature using electrical
heaters. The data acquired have been processed using SEISAN software.
During this expedition i.e., from January 2005 to February 2006, continuous
seismic data have been recorded and archived and stored in CDs for further
processing and analysis.
Using SEISAN software the final analysis of this data collected up to
December 2005 has been completed and reported to International
Seismological Centre, United Kingdom. The data acquisition during
wintering period, the Preliminary Determination of Epicenters (PDE) reports
by NEIC are referred to while processing the data using SEISAN 7.2,
PCSUDS and REFTEK utilities software. After completion of the analysis,
the arrival times, origin times and the corresponding hypo central parameters
of the processed events were used to compile the MAITRI Seismological
